subject.title: Expose structured progress metrics in hook events for plugin-based live progress cards

question: Should OpenClaw add structured progress metrics to public plugin hook events, and which runtime source owns step totals, percent, ETA, and terminal success/failure semantics across producers?
rationale: This would be an additive public Plugin SDK contract, and naive tool-call counting could mislead plugin UIs for dynamic, retried, cancelled, failed, or branched runs.

options.title: Define a narrow metrics contract
options.body: Add optional metrics only where producers can supply authoritative values, leave unknowns absent, and document/test the hook semantics across producers.

options.title: Keep current hook payloads
options.body: Leave plugins to derive phase or text progress from existing events until OpenClaw has a stronger progress source of truth.

options.title: Design a dedicated progress event
options.body: Create a separate progress event or agent-event projection instead of attaching percentages to tool and terminal hooks.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow metrics contract
recommendation.body: Add optional metrics only where producers can supply authoritative values, leave unknowns absent, and document/test the hook semantics across producers.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-history trail for public hook contract changes points to this owner path, and the decision affects Plugin SDK semantics.
